https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cj4k.text: Image source, UK Ministry of Defence Image caption, Iran said two Su-24 fighter jets were used in the mission on a Qatari military base on 2 March 2026 (file photo) By Matt Spivey Published 3 hours ago Iran has called for the release of three Iranian pilots it said were captured by Qatar after two fighter jets were hit by air defences during a military operation at the start of the US-Iran war. In a letter to the head of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), Iran's Brig Gen Mohammad Bagherzadeh said the pilots - Javad Salehi, Abdul Majid Dashtian, and Imran Behroshian - had been held captive for six months. He said the body of a fourth pilot, Majid Kazemi, was returned after he was killed in the same operation on 2 March 2026 - the third day of the war. Qatar "categorically denied" Iran's claims and said it was "surprised by these misleading statements". Gen Bagherzadeh said the three pilots had been captured by Qatar after they ejected from their jets during the combat mission on a Qatari military base. In the letter to ICRC chief Mirjana Spoljaric, published by Iranian media, he accused Qatar of violating "the inalienable rights of these prisoners, contrary to all international laws and regulations". The letter also claimed the three pilots had not been allowed to meet or contact their families. Qatar's foreign affairs spokesperson Majed Mohammed Al Ansari said contact had been made with the pilots "after they violated Qatari airspace", but it did not receive a response. "The necessary measures were taken to defend our territory in accordance with international law," he added in a statement on X. Al Ansari said Qatar's search and rescue teams "carried out their duties to the fullest extent in searching for the pilots' remains". He said Qatar contacted Iran to "co-ordinate the handover of the remains of one of the pilots that were recovered", and that Tehran had yet to respond to an invitation to review details of the search and rescue operation. https://www.bursa.ro/democracy-under-gua.text: Only a few days after the scandal caused by the new ANI law and CCR Decision no. 883/2026, which paved the way for the termination of the mandates of some local elected officials based on a regulation subsequent to the sanctioned acts, the Permanent Electoral Authority proposes a new law on political parties, through which it requests almost the entire administrative power over their establishment, operation, reorganization and dissolution. The two situations do not have the same legal object, but they seem to indicate the same trend: limiting the effects of the vote and transferring the decision from voters to unelected authorities. If the ANI legislation allows intervention after the vote, to terminate the mandate of an elected official, the AEP project creates the instruments through which the political framework can be controlled before the citizen reaches the polls. The institution led by Adrian Ţuţuianu would decide who can establish a party, what documents are accepted, whether statutory amendments are legal, whether the formation is still active and whether it should be dissolved. The current president of AEP is not a technocrat with no political past, but a former president of the Dâmboviţa County Council, senator, Minister of Defense and an important leader of the PSD. The fact that he is no longer a member of the party does not erase this biography or the legitimate questions raised by the project. It is at least curious that an institution led by a former leader of a party that was frequently in government would request the right to decide administratively on the legal birth and death of all political formations, including those that compete with the PSD. There is no evidence that the project aims to favor a party, but the laws must also be analyzed in terms of how the powers granted can be used by the current or future leaders of the institution. The project is not limited to digitizing registers. The AEP would take over from the Bucharest Tribunal the party and alliance registers, files, archives and databases, verify the founders, statutes, programs, headquarters, names and permanent signs, decide on the registration or rejection of a party, approve subsequent amendments and ascertain cases of dissolution. Currently, the registration of a party is decided by the Bucharest Tribunal. The project transfers the competence to panels made up of five AEP employees, declared "independent” by law. However, they are appointed by the institution, work within it and do not even pronounce the final decision: they draw up a report and formulate a proposal, and the decision is made by the AEP. The independence of the panels stops, therefore, exactly where the real power begins. The AEP decision will be able to be challenged at the Bucharest Court of Appeal within ten days of publication. Access to justice does not disappear, but it is moved after the exercise of administrative power. Instead of the court deciding on the establishment of the party, the party will first have to obtain the approval of the AEP and only after rejection will it be able to request the intervention of the judge. More seriously, the AEP will be able to initiate proceedings in cases of dissolution and it will also issue the decision. The institution will ascertain the alleged misconduct, initiate the procedure, handle it through its own employees and decide to dissolve the party. It will be simultaneously a controller, a notification authority and a decision-making authority, and the court will intervene only if the party challenges the decision within the deadline. One of the most controversial texts is art. 56 para. (7). If the statutory amendments are not communicated to the AEP or are definitively rejected, and the party continues to act on their basis, the Authority orders the dissolution of the party, considering that its purpose or activity has become illicit or contrary to public order. The provision is strikingly reminiscent of the conflict in the PNL, in which the decisions of an extraordinary congress were later annulled by the court. If the project had already become law, the dispute could have reached the courts only after the AEP, led by former social democrat Adrian Ţuţuianu, had ordered the dissolution of the PNL. It is not clear how the failure to register a statutory amendment automatically turns the party's purpose into an illicit one. Between the procedural deviation and dissolution, there should be gradual sanctions: notification, a period of remediation, a fine or suspension of the effects of the amendment. The project jumps straight to the maximum sanction and uses the notion of public order to give it a legal appearance. The AEP will also be able to establish the inactivity of a party that has not organized a general assembly for four years, has not renewed its leadership, has not updated its headquarters, has not submitted financial statements, has prevented the control of financing or has not designated candidates for two successive elections. The phrase "two successive elections” is ambiguous. It is not specified whether they must be elections of the same type - local, parliamentary or European Parliament, or any two elections. A party interested only in local elections could be declared inactive because it does not participate in presidential and parliamentary elections? Does a regional party have to participate in the European Parliament elections in order to continue to exist? The legislative project does not answer. Another change concerns the number of founders. After the CCR declared the 25,000 person threshold unconstitutional, the current law allows the establishment of a party by three members. AEP proposes a minimum of 100 founders, representing both sexes. The threshold is over 33 times higher than the current one, without the explanatory statement showing how many fictitious parties were established, what problems they caused and why exactly 100 founders are necessary. The representativeness of a party should be verified by voting, not before establishment. Legal personality does not guarantee mandates, subsidies or access to Parliament. The formation must separately fulfill the electoral conditions and convince voters. Raising the threshold does not protect democracy, but makes it more difficult for new competitors to emerge. The draft law also grants the AEP extensive powers over names and permanent signs. Words likely to create confusion with authorities or public institutions are prohibited, such as "authority”, "guard”, "academy”, "institute”, "university”, "chamber”, "bar” and "others like that”. Preventing confusion is legitimate, but the open-ended formula "others like that” allows the AEP to supplement the prohibitions through administrative practice. Even the protection of names and symbols does not sufficiently clarify the situation of satire, parody, civic campaigns and content published on social networks. The draft law also stipulates that party members must act with professionalism, meritocracy, honesty and integrity, correctly inform voters and respect fair political competition. As ethical principles, the requirements are natural. As legal obligations that can justify sanctioning or exclusion, they are dangerously vague. It is not explained who determines what political professionalism, meritocracy or correct information means. A critical member could be accused of harming the party, and a wrong opinion could be qualified as false information. While the AEP expands its power, parties are given very short deadlines and fines between 20,000 and 80,000 lei. Some documents must be communicated within only three days. For a parliamentary party, the fine is bearable; for a small formation, it may mean the cessation of activity. The most dangerous transitional provision obliges all existing parties and alliances to amend their statutes, programs or protocols within six months. Failure to comply with the deadline becomes a reason for dissolution for inactivity. Thus, a legal, active and electorally participating party can be dissolved simply for not adapting its documents on time. There is no mandatory warning procedure and no additional deadline for remedy: administrative delay is treated as political disappearance. Articol despre AEP, Adrian tutuianu, PSD, political parties law.

https://www.budapesttimes.hu/hungary/gov.text: The Budapest Times Government axes public service university’s teacher training, citing political meddling Teacher training at the National University of Public Service is to be discontinued — announced the Minister of Education at the ceremonial, public senate session marking the start of the academic year at the University of Debrecen on Sunday. The cabinet is breaking with the divisive policies of the previous government, which resulted in teacher training becoming fragmented, said Judit Lannert. She added that, as part of this, teacher training will be “withdrawn” from the National University of Public Service, and that work is currently under way to establish a fair and lawful process for carrying this out. At the remaining training institutions, they are supporting the development of a unified, transparent, and high-quality teacher training programme that builds on the values of Hungarian higher education while meeting the demands of the 21st century, the minister said. According to the minister, the divisive policies of the previous government were felt particularly acutely in teacher training. “While politics encroached on this area and eroded the autonomy of institutions, an increasing number of unjustified differences emerged in the way programmes operated under differing training and exit requirements.” She added that this had not only created uncertainty for teacher training institutions and students, but had also undermined the overall standing of the teaching profession and the uniform quality of training. Judit Lannert said that in the future, theoretical and practical knowledge required for the effective support of students with special educational needs, integration, learning and behavioural difficulties, as well as students from different social backgrounds, will be strengthened across all areas of teacher training. The Minister of Education identified it as a priority goal that many talented and dedicated young people should once again choose the teaching profession, for which the right conditions must be created. The minister described the renewal of teacher training as one of the most important issues for the future of Hungarian education. She indicated, among other things, that the still overly complicated admissions process would be simplified, on which the ministry will soon initiate consultations, and that they are counting on the partnership of experts in Debrecen as well. Judit Lannert also touched on the fact that today higher education institutions operate under so many different models that it is already hampering transparency and effective regulation. She indicated that inequalities between state-maintained and foundation-maintained universities are being continuously eliminated, that values will be preserved, and that “where they see weakness, they will make changes.” Starting from the 2027–28 academic year, a more unified and equitable funding model will be introduced, along with an operating framework in which the roles of the governing body, the senate, and the rector are clearly defined — she said, indicating that academic freedom and institutional autonomy will be restored at the legislative level, and that fundamental rights will be reinstated in the higher education act. Addressing students, she said they will strengthen student-centredness, review the issues of housing and scholarships, seek to increase equal opportunities, and strive to provide support for protecting students’ mental wellbeing. Judit Lannert spoke approvingly of the work of the University of Debrecen, calling the institution one of the most important universities in Hungary, one that “is of outstanding significance for the new government.” She added that the university had been a pioneer in successfully “attracting” foreign students, which serves as an exemplary model for other universities. https://www.dw.com/en/south-korea-lost-s.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5NUty The shark has been nicknamed 'Bukangi,' after the Korean name for Busan's North Port Image: Yonhap/REUTERS Advertisement A shark stranded in a canal in the northern port city of Busan has become South Korea 's latest celebrity, tourist magnet and ambassador, as authorities' attempts to guide it back out to sea have so far faltered. What do we know about the stranded shark? The shark was first spotted in a narrow waterway in Busan's North Port on September 18. Reports on its possible species vary but seem to suggest it's a type of requiem shark, possibly a bull shark or a bronze whaler. It's a fairly large shark, appearing to be roughly 3.5 meters (around 11 feet, 6 inches) long. It's been nicknamed "Bukangi," derived from the Korean name for the North Port in Busan, Buk Hang. Attempts to encourage the animal back out to sea earlier this week failed Image: Son Hyung-joo/Yonhap/AP Photo/picture alliance Trapped aquatic tourist trap Busan city authorities say roughly 600,000 people have flocked to see the creature over the past two weeks. During the four-day Chuseok bank holiday weekend, Busan city authorities said that almost half a million people visited the waterfront park where the shark was stranded, compared to an average of around 2,000 visitors on weekends. City Mayor Chun Jae-soo thanked the involuntary visitor for publicity that would otherwise have cost "trillions." Local media reported a spike in sales of shark-shaped ice creams at nearby stores. The city named the lost predator an honorary ambassador after 91% of participants in a social media poll approved of the notion. Shares in the Pinkfong Company, the studio behind the viral "Baby Shark" song, also rose by around 7% at one point amid the hype. The excitement has also led to false rumors of a second sighting, or even of it being the shark's own spawn, with AI-generated dross inevitably following. Visitors flocked to the park in the North Port over the long bank holiday weekend to see the stranded sea creature Image: Son Hyung-joo/Yonhap/AP Photo/picture alliance How are authorities trying to guide it back out to sea? A rescue operation earlier this week failed. The Coast Guard and other agencies deployed vessels that sprayed jets of water behind the shark, trying to encourage it to swim back towards the ocean. Instead the shark simply evaded the streams without heading in the desired direction. South Korea's Chosun Daily newspaper reported that a fresh attempt, this time seeking to use a net to guide the shark out, was being planned for Friday. The shark is the latest unlikely animal celebrity craze to grip South Korea, not least following the excitement in April over Neukgu, a young wolf that escaped from a zoo. It spent nine days at large before being recaptured. The incident is also somewhat reminiscent of the German frenzy this year over a beached humpback whale , who was in turn given the place-based nickname of "Timmy" — after the Timmendorfer Strand beach on the Baltic coast, the site of its first stranding. https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/poland-beavers.text: A warning sign about beaver damage in a Polish forest was reportedly brought down by beavers themselves after the animals gnawed through its wooden post, according to local foresters. Images of the fallen sign have circulated widely online, with users seizing on the irony of a beaver‑warning notice apparently undone by the very creatures it described.The episode has sparked a wave of jokes about an apparent beaver 'rebellion' and prompted puzzled reactions over why wood was chosen as the supporting material, given the animals' well‑known taste for timber.Beavers Bring Down Their Own Warning SignThe incident took place at the Lubliniec Forestry District in Silesia, southern Poland, where foresters had installed a sign beside a pond in the Łopian forest district.The sign carried the Polish warning 'Uwaga! Szkody wyrządzone przez bobry', which translates to 'Warning! Damage caused by beavers.'However, photographs shared by the forestry district showed the wooden post had been gnawed through, leaving the sign lying on the ground.The warning was not merely precautionary. According to the foresters, beavers in the area had been digging burrows beneath a road and felling trees around the pond, potentially creating hazards for people nearby.The forestry district described the incident with humour, suggesting the beavers did not want people to be warned about their activities. It also advised visitors to exercise caution and jokingly suggested they imagine the warning sign was still there if they spotted a gnawed piece of wood sticking out of the ground.'Ungovernable Beavers' Spark Wave of Online QuipsThe incident has prompted social media users to poke fun at the irony of using a wooden post to warn people about animals known for gnawing through wood.One commenter offered a personal take, writing, 'Ungovernable beavers were the bane of my younger years.'The jokes also took a political turn, with another user commenting, 'Beavers as opposition is not something I need right now.'Others imagined the animals' actions as the beginning of a full-scale uprising against human authority.Fallen Sign Becomes the Butt of the Joke Not everyone was ready to surrender to the supposed beaver rebellion. Some commenters instead offered tongue-in-cheek solutions to the fallen sign.One X user pointed out that the remaining post might still be useful, writing, 'Well at least the end is pointy so they can hammer it back in the ground.'The reactions reflect the central absurdity of the incident: a warning about beaver damage was itself brought down by what appeared to be beaver activity.Why Polish Foresters Warn About BeaversAlthough the story has provided plenty of material for jokes, the warning addressed a genuine safety concern.Beavers can fell trees and dig burrows into riverbanks and areas beneath roads. These activities can undermine the ground or leave weakened trees that may fall, posing risks to people and infrastructure.The animals also play an important ecological role. Their dams can retain water and create wetland habitats that support other wildlife, although their activities can sometimes conflict with human land use.For the foresters in Lubliniec, the incident offered an unusually fitting illustration of the problem they were trying to highlight. Their warning sign was intended to alert people to beaver damage, but the animals reportedly left the message on the ground.
